title: Make completed-trace archive cleanup part of the pipeline

approvedRows.question: DTR-post-commit-archive-pipeline
approvedRows.currentState: Completed traces can remain open and hot after implementation evidence is accepted and committed; archive cleanup is manual.
approvedRows.desiredState: Completed trace cleanup is a first-class post-commit pipeline step that closes and compacts completed traces with a restore ref.
approvedRows.rationale: Hot trace state should show active work only while Git preserves full completed trace history for audit and hydration.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users see a smaller active queue and can still restore closed trace detail when needed.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers get a repeatable lifecycle step instead of remembering manual cleanup after each commit.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Requires trace retention API, tests, docs, and pipeline quality wiring.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: The request matches current CodeWiki trace-retention direction and fixes a visible lifecycle gap.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: Matches user request to make post-commit archive cleanup part of the CodeWiki pipeline.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Keeps trace truth hot only while preserving recoverability through Git restore refs.
agentAssessment.rationale: No lower-cost option prevents completed-open trace buildup while keeping hydration possible.

approvedRows.safetyBoundary: Archive automation may only run after implementation evidence exits and a git restore ref is available; it must not delete unrecoverable trace records.
failureModes: Compacting a trace before implementation completes would hide active work.
Using a wrong git restore ref would make hydration unsafe.
Leaving completed traces open keeps stale hot queue noise.
approvedRows.negativeTestPlan: Add tests that block compacting incomplete traces, reject hydration with mismatched restore refs, and enforce archive disposition in Implementation quality when required.
approvedRows.compatibilityImpact: Existing manual wiki_archive close remains available; new compact/sweep behavior must preserve current trace replay and hydration contracts.

approvedRows.question: DTR-hot-stub-hydration-contract
approvedRows.currentState: Retention stubs and hydration plans exist as preview helpers, but completed trace files are not compacted into a hot stub form.
approvedRows.desiredState: Closed completed traces can be represented by a minimal hot stub that records head, close metadata, restore ref, and hydration refs while full records remain recoverable from Git.
approvedRows.rationale: A hot stub gives current state enough metadata without making the working tree carry every completed trace body forever.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users can distinguish active traces from archived traces and request hydration when old detail is needed.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers can keep repository trace views light without losing audit history.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Requires retention model/API tests and view compatibility checks.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: Hot stub plus git restore ref is the needed bridge between cleanup and recoverability.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: Matches user requirement to archive in git with hydration/restoration possible.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Separates hot state from retained history while keeping trace-backed guarantees.
agentAssessment.rationale: A minimal stub avoids central indexes and follows existing no-catalog retention design.

approvedRows.safetyBoundary: Stub compaction must preserve trace_head and trace_close replay validity and must validate archived records during hydration.
failureModes: Invalid parent references could make compact stubs unreplayable.
Stub metadata could diverge from archived records.
Views could treat archived traces as active work.
approvedRows.negativeTestPlan: Add tests for compact record replay, retention stub refs, hydration mismatch, and wiki_state ignoring closed compact traces as active work.
approvedRows.compatibilityImpact: Existing closed full trace files remain valid; compact stubs are an additional valid representation.

approvedRows.question: DTR-implementation-archive-quality-standard
approvedRows.currentState: Implementation quality can pass without any archive disposition for completed traces.
approvedRows.desiredState: Implementation quality can enforce an archive disposition when policy requires post-commit trace cleanup, so completion cannot silently leave trace-retention work unplanned.
approvedRows.rationale: False completion includes lifecycle cleanup omissions, not only code/test failures.
approvedRows.userImpact: Users get a pipeline that closes work end-to-end instead of stopping at commit.
approvedRows.maintainerImpact: Maintainers get a quality gate and explicit skip reason when archive cleanup is intentionally deferred.
approvedRows.routeRationale: Requires Implementation input/output type changes, quality standard wiring, tests, and docs.
approvedRows.recommendationRationale: This addresses the user's enforcement suggestion while keeping post-commit restore-ref timing explicit.

agentAssessment.userAlignment: Matches user request that pipeline cleanup can be enforced in Implementation loop quality.
agentAssessment.projectBenefit: Adds false-pass resistance for completed-open traces.
agentAssessment.rationale: A policy-controlled quality standard avoids forcing impossible pre-commit archive writes while requiring disposition planning.

approvedRows.safetyBoundary: Quality enforcement must not require a git restore ref before commit, but must require a concrete post-commit archive plan or an explicit retained-hot reason.
failureModes: Requiring a commit SHA too early would deadlock Implementation.
Allowing silent skips would preserve current false pass.
Forcing archive for intentionally hot traces could hide active follow-up work.
approvedRows.negativeTestPlan: Add positive and negative Implementation quality tests for required archive disposition, explicit retain-hot reason, and missing disposition blocking.
approvedRows.compatibilityImpact: Default behavior should preserve existing callers unless archive disposition is required by config or facade input.
